# Mouse Events on Canvas

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Mouse Events on Canvas

In Chapter 3 the ball moves on its own. Now the player joins.

In Brick Breaker the paddle follows the mouse. Wherever the cursor moves, the paddle moves with it. Simple idea, but there is one step most people miss. The browser reports mouse position relative to the whole page, not the canvas. So before you can use it, you need to convert it.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3canvas.addEventListener("mousemove", (e) =>  {
4    const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
5    const mouseX = e.clientX - rect.left;
6    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
7    ctx.fillRect(mouseX - 50, 260, 100, 12);
8}
9);
10ctx.fillRect(150, 260, 100, 12);
```

Click Run Code then move your mouse over the canvas and you will see the paddle follow your cursor.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Here, getBoundingClientRect() returns the canvas element's position relative to the viewport. Subtracting rect.left from e.clientX converts the browser's page coordinate into a canvas-local coordinate. Move the mouse over the canvas and the paddle follows.

The conversion pattern is the same every time:

```javascriptDOM
const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect(); const x = e.clientX - rect.left; const y = e.clientY - rect.top;
```

Always use getBoundingClientRect() for this conversion . Never hardcode the canvas offset. If the page scrolls, the canvas moves inside a flex container, or the layout shifts, getBoundingClientRect() still gives the correct position. A hardcoded offset breaks the moment anything on the page changes. In Brick Breaker, you will clamp mouseX so the paddle cannot slide off the canvas edges.

![Diagram showing e.clientX measured from viewport left and canvas rect.left, with the subtraction giving canvas-local x](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

Next, you will learn how to handle keyboard input so arrow keys can move the paddle too.
